newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: The French 10-year bond future set a new historic contract high on Tuesday for the third straight trading day, then retraced to settle off its best levels.
The market was supported by a firm performance by the Bund and the U.S. T-Bond and analysts said it appeared poised to advance further on Wednesday.
The bond future touched an all-time high of 131.80 before retracing to settle at 131.64, up 18 basis points.
Sogeposte analyst Rachid Medjaoui said the future could hit 132.00, possibly rising to 132.50. After that, he said he was "not negative but more neutral to slightly bearish".

Analysts said the main factor driving the market was the United States. Some urged caution before a batch of U.S. figures due on Friday but others were sanguine, saying they saw no inflationary pressures in the pipeline. "There's an absence of inflationary pressures," said one.

Figures showing a rise in consumer confidence in January to its best level in more than a year had no market impact. National statistic institute INSEE's global confidence indicator rose in January to minus 30 from minus 33 in December. The seasonally adjusted index has been edging higher since hitting a nine-month low of minus 37 in May 1996.
"The figures conform withour scenario that (economic) activity is picking up but not very strongly," said economist Serge Le Gal of Caisse des Depots.
A trader said there was some non-resident buying and that domestic insurers, traditional strong supports of the French bond market, were "confidently buying paper."
On the cash market, the yield on the OAT 6.50 government bond fell to 5.41 percent from 5.45 percent. The spread with the equivalent German Bund remained steady.
